title: Geometric optimality of entanglement-induced fast qubit reset
authors: Davide Rinaldi, Mattia Moroder, Dario Gerace, Giacomo Guarnieri, Steve Campbell
abstract: Fast and reliable qubit reset is essential for the efficient operation of quantum processors. Among the proposed strategies, Mpemba-effect-based protocols offer a simple route to accelerated relaxation, but provide limited insight into the optimality of the full reset dynamics. Geometric approaches, by contrast, quantify optimality but do not generally suggest practical acceleration protocols. Here, we bridge these perspectives through a geometric analysis of entanglement-assisted qubit reset. We show that entangling operations can redistribute local coherences across a multi-qubit register, allowing the reduced state of each qubit to follow a geodesic path towards the ground state. Remarkably, this locally optimal behaviour can emerge even when the collective evolution becomes suboptimal in the full state space. We illustrate this interplay for different families of initial multi-qubit states. Our results provide a geometric perspective on Mpemba-inspired reset acceleration and clarify when extending two-qubit protocols to larger registers provides a further advantage in the reset process.
summary: This work analyzes fast qubit reset by applying geometric principles to the state space of multi-qubit systems. It demonstrates that entanglement can accelerate reset by ensuring that individual qubit states follow optimal geodesic paths, even if the overall system evolution is not globally optimal. This offers a powerful geometric tool for designing better quantum processors.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for fast and reliable qubit reset protocols, aiming to understand the optimality of the full reset dynamics beyond simple asymptotic decay models.
main_result: Entangling operations can induce a faster reset time (Mpemba effect) by allowing the reduced state of each qubit to follow a geodesic path, even if the collective evolution in the full state space is suboptimal.
method: The authors employ a geometric analysis using the Hilbert-Schmidt metric to quantify state evolution speed and compare the actual path length to the theoretical geodesic path length.
model_or_system: The system involves N qubits undergoing dissipative evolution, modeled by a Lindbladian master equation. The analysis compares the dynamics of initial, entangled, and ground states in the multi-qubit density matrix space.
key_observables: Reset time ($	au$), geodesic path length ($L_{	ext{geo}}$), distinguishability measures ($d(t)$), and the ratio of actual to geodesic speed ($	au/	au_a$).
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_\phi$), number of qubits ($N$), and the initial state structure (e.g., GHZ or W states).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the HS metric defining the geometry of the state space, and it compares total-space evolution against locally optimal reduced-space evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of state paths, comparing initial vs. entangled states, showing the Mpemba crossing, and detailing the coherence evolution of single qubits relative to the geodesic.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (fast reset), introduces the geometric framework (HS metric, geodesics), analyzes the dynamics using specific entangled states (W/GHZ), and concludes by comparing local vs. global optimality.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous geometric framework to analyze transient quantum dynamics, linking concepts like quantum speed limits and the Mpemba effect to the structure of the state space, which is highly relevant for designing optimal quantum control protocols.
